page: The Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Compute resources are provisioned on a burstable CPU allocation model, backed by a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16) and AMX (Tile, INT8). The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, delivering 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local instance storage or onboard discrete GPUs, relying on remote network storage and delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong general-purpose and vectorized processing capability. The instance demonstrates solid multi-core compute throughput, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 18040.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 51713.67, both landing in the top 25%. Instruction-level optimizations yield top 10% performance in Geekbench text processing (2875.0) and top 25% performance in single- and multi-threaded compression (34.31 GB/sec in gzip, 224.86 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression). Memory-intensive tests show a large block read throughput of 175.61 GB/sec and write throughput of 77.15 GB/sec, placing memory bandwidth in the middle 50% relative to broader cloud benchmarks.

In terms of workload-specific evaluation, the m8i-flex.8xlarge excels at static web serving (58.6 GB/sec) and in-memory key-value processing, achieving 62.33 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-based machine learning inference with small models performs competitively, reaching 350.71 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model. However, scaling to large language models exposes CPU architectural limits, yielding 2.75 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model. The combination of a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, burstable compute model, and AMX support makes this instance cost-efficient for web serving, microservices, application servers, build jobs, and lightweight inference tasks that do not require dedicated full-time CPU saturation or local NVMe storage.
description: The Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. It features 32 burstable vCPUs (16 physical cores), 128.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, and a 480 MB L3 cache, alongside AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions. The instance omits local disks and discrete GPUs, featuring an 8 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmarks reveal strong integer, text processing, and compression throughput, alongside capable in-memory data processing, recording 62.33 million Redis SET operations per second and 58.6 GB/sec web serving throughput. CPU-based small model inference is responsive, though larger models reflect CPU-bound limits. It provides resource balance and cost efficiency for web applications, microservices, and general backend workloads.
